title: Enriched counit bar mapping totalization and composition
statement:
Use coherent diagrams, nerves, mapping spaces and limiting or colimiting cones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the cochain convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and enriched categories in the complete-algebroid sense of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Put $\mathcal V=\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$, and let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be tensored $\mathcal V$-enriched categories in sufficiently large universes. Suppose $L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:U$ is an enriched adjunction with unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$, whose functors preserve tensors coherently and whose unit and counit respect these comparisons. Set $T=UL$, $\mu=U\epsilon L$. Suppose $\mathcal D$ admits small geometric realizations, $U$ preserves them and reflects equivalences, and mapping out of a geometric realization in $\mathcal D$ gives the corresponding homotopy limit in $\mathcal V$. Here a geometric realization is the colimit of a coherent diagram on $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$, where $\Delta$ consists of finite nonempty ordered sets and monotone maps; derived totalization is the coherent limit on $N(\Delta)$.

For $X,Y\in\mathcal D$, put $A=UX$, $B=UY$ with induced $T$-actions $a=U\epsilon_X$, $b=U\epsilon_Y$. There is a natural equivalence of mapping objects
$$\mathcal D(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}^{\mathbf R}_{[r]\in\Delta}\mathcal C(T^r A,B).$$
The entire cosimplicial object is obtained by applying $\mathcal D(-,Y)$ to the counit bar $B_rX=LT^rUX$ and then the enriched adjunction. Its two endpoint cofaces use the actions on $A$ and $B$, interior cofaces use $\mu$, and codegeneracies use $\eta$, with all coherence homotopies. The equivalence is induced by the augmentation $B_\bullet X\to X$ and preserves coherent composition and units. On the totalizations, composition is the operation induced by the bar diagonal: a word is split into initial and final subwords, the functor $T$ is applied to the first mapping component as required, and the resulting components are composed in $\mathcal C$. More precisely its pair of word-length components $f:T^pA\to B$ and $g:T^qB\to C$ has word-length $p+q$ component $g\circ T^q(f):T^{p+q}A\to C$, using the enriched tensor comparison to interpret this as a morphism of mapping objects. Splittings into three or more consecutive subwords, and insertions of empty subwords, supply the associative and unital higher compatibilities. This is a statement about derived totalizations, not ordinary equalizers or uncompleted direct-sum total complexes.

proof.text: Forget enrichment temporarily. The enriched adjunction gives an adjunction of underlying enhanced categories. The hypotheses on realizations, preservation and reflection are precisely those of [lem-coef-infinity-monadic-bar]. Apply its bar-realization assertion, not just its comparison assertion: the coherent augmented diagram $P_rX=L T^r A$ has colimit $X$. Faces contract adjacent $LU$ by the counit, degeneracies insert $L\eta U$, and the augmentation is the iterated counit. These are natural in $X$. Thus the simplicial object used below is an actual coherent bar, including all higher simplices.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: middle derived coefficient adjunction; agent expansion by the enriched counit bar (steps below), not an argument supplied by this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: For each $r$, the assumed enriched adjunction gives $\Psi_r:\mathcal D(LT^rA,Y)\simeq\mathcal C(T^rA,B)$, with $\Psi_r(h)=U(h)\eta_{T^rA}$ and inverse $f\mapsto\epsilon_Y L(f)$. The two composites reduce to identities by naturality of $\eta,\epsilon$ and the two adjunction triangles. These formulas are morphisms of mapping objects: use enriched composition and the coherent tensor comparisons in the hypotheses. Apply this natural equivalence to the whole diagram $\mathcal D(P_\bullet X,Y)$ from step 1. Naturality on every simplex, rather than only on faces in the homotopy category, supplies a coherent cosimplicial diagram $H^r(A,B)=\mathcal C(T^rA,B)$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: middle derived coefficient adjunction; agent expansion by the enriched counit bar (steps below), not an argument supplied by this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: Here are all its generating operators. For $f:T^rA\to B$, the cofaces into degree $r+1$ are $d^0f=bT(f)$, $d^if=f\,T^{i-1}(\mu_{T^{r-i}A})$ for $1\leq i\leq r$, and $d^{r+1}f=f\,T^r(a)$. For $r\geq1$, its codegeneracies are $s^if=f\,T^i(\eta_{T^{r-i-1}A})$ for $0\leq i<r$. Indeed, conjugate each counit contraction or unit insertion in step 1 by $\Psi$. The outermost counit becomes $U\epsilon_Y=b$, an interior counit becomes $U\epsilon L=\mu$, and the last counit becomes $U\epsilon_X=a$. Unit insertions become $\eta$. Since this is conjugation of the coherent diagram of step 2, the formulas carry its specified coherence homotopies; no claim that strict simplicial identities alone construct those homotopies is needed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: middle derived coefficient adjunction; agent expansion by the enriched counit bar (steps below), not an argument supplied by this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: By the mapping-out-of-realization hypothesis, the augmentation induces an equivalence $\mathcal D(X,Y)\simeq\lim_{[r]\in\Delta}\mathcal D(P_rX,Y)$ in $\mathcal V$. Apply the natural termwise equivalences of step 2 to this limiting cone. They and their inverse give inverse equivalences of cone categories, so preserve terminal cones. The result is $\alpha_{X,Y}:\mathcal D(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}^{\mathbf R}H^\bullet(A,B)$. It is natural in $X,Y$, since both the augmentation and the adjunction are natural. This uses precisely the coherent limiting-cone meaning of totalization and does not replace it by an equalizer or an underived total complex.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: middle derived coefficient adjunction; agent expansion by the enriched counit bar (steps below), not an argument supplied by this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: Write $a^{[0]}=1_A$ and $a^{[r+1]}=a\,T(a^{[r]}):T^{r+1}A\to A$; define $b^{[r]}$ similarly. The module associativity and unit coherences are obtained by applying $U$ to counit naturality and the adjunction triangles. In particular $a^{[q]}T^q(a^{[p]})\simeq a^{[p+q]}$, with all iterated versions. The $r$-th component of the augmentation equivalence applied to $F:X\to Y$ is $\alpha_r(F)=U(F)a^{[r]}$. To check this, the degree-$r$ augmentation has underlying map $a^{[r+1]}$; taking its adjoint precomposes with $\eta_{T^rA}$ and cancels the first action by the unit law. The same calculation is valid with a parameter $M\in\mathcal V$: a map $M\to\mathcal D(X,Y)$ is evaluation $F:M\otimes X\to Y$, and its component is $U(F)(1_M\otimes a^{[r]})$, using $U(M\otimes X)\simeq M\otimes A$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: middle derived coefficient adjunction; agent expansion by the enriched counit bar (steps below), not an argument supplied by this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text:
Check the claimed word splitting on mapping objects, including parameters. Put $E=\mathcal D(X,Y)$, $F=\mathcal D(Y,Z)$, and $C=UZ$. Let $u:E\otimes A\to B$ and $v:F\otimes B\to C$ be the images under $U$ of the universal evaluation maps. Counit naturality, also for these parameterized evaluations, gives $b^{[q]}T^q(u)\simeq u(1_E\otimes a^{[q]})$, with the tensor comparison understood. The $p$- and $q$-components from step 5 are $u_p=u(1_E\otimes a^{[p]})$ and $v_q=v(1_F\otimes b^{[q]})$. Their proposed split-word composite is the map
$$F\otimes E\otimes T^{p+q}A\longrightarrow F\otimes T^q(E\otimes T^pA)\xrightarrow{1_F\otimes T^q(u_p)}F\otimes T^qB\xrightarrow{v_q}C.$$
The first arrow is the inverse tensor comparison. Substitute the displayed action compatibility and then $a^{[q]}T^q(a^{[p]})\simeq a^{[p+q]}$. The result is $v(1_F\otimes u)(1_F\otimes1_E\otimes a^{[p+q]})$, exactly the $(p+q)$-component of $\alpha_{X,Z}$ of enriched composition. Universal evaluation and currying make this an equality with specified homotopy of morphisms in $\mathcal V$, not just a check on degree-zero elements. The action compatibilities used here are the given naturality homotopies and their higher simplices.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: middle derived coefficient adjunction; agent expansion by the enriched counit bar (steps below), not an argument supplied by this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text:
For clarity, existence and coherence of the operation on totalizations do not follow from a bare list of component formulas. Denote their objects by $Q_{XY}$ and choose inverse equivalences $\beta_{XY}$ of $\alpha_{XY}$. Define
$$m_Q=\alpha_{XZ}\,m_{\mathcal D}(\beta_{YZ}\otimes\beta_{XY}):Q_{YZ}\otimes Q_{XY}\to Q_{XZ}.$$
Step 6 computes every consecutive-word cut of this actual morphism: after precomposing by the equivalence $\alpha_{YZ}\otimes\alpha_{XY}$, the cut $(p,q)$ is $g\,T^q(f)$. Precomposition by that equivalence has inverse precomposition by $\beta_{YZ}\otimes\beta_{XY}$, so this calculation determines the morphism and the compatible homotopies on the whole parameter space. Varying a cut contracts adjacent letters by $\mu$ or an endpoint action; their compatibility is exactly the action naturality in step 6. Inserting a unit uses the same unit homotopy. Consequently $m_Q$ realizes the bar-diagonal operation on coherent totalizations: consecutive subwords, including empty ones, give its components and homotopies. This specifies the operation intrinsically via the augmentation and verifies the stated formula, rather than assuming an independent existence theorem for a diagonal on an ordinary total complex.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: middle derived coefficient adjunction; agent expansion by the enriched counit bar (steps below), not an argument supplied by this blueprint paragraph.

proof.text: The unit is $e_{Q,X}=\alpha_{XX}(1_X)$, whose degree-$r$ component is $a^{[r]}$. For three word components $f:T^pA\to B$, $g:T^qB\to C$, $h:T^rC\to D$, both successive splittings give $h\,T^r(g)\,T^{r+q}(f)$. Functoriality of $T$, the associative composition in the given enrichment, and its coherent tensor comparisons provide the comparison, including parameters. For arbitrarily many factors apply the same evaluation to the consecutive blocks of the word; refinement of a partition is functorial substitution, and empty blocks use the identity and the module unit coherence. Equivalently these are the higher associativity and unit simplices of $m_{\mathcal D}$ in the explicit formula of step 7, with each adjacent $\beta\alpha$ canceled by its inverse-equivalence homotopy. Thus every higher compatibility, not only the binary formula, is retained. These formulas show that $\alpha$ preserves coherent composition and units. No convergence, boundedness or sum/product interchange is used at any point.
